subproblem.title: Mollification of a Lipschitz function: smooth, same gradient bound, uniformly close, local (Simon's f^(σ))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0, g : ℝ^P → ℝ K-Lipschitz and σ > 0. Then there is a C^∞ function g' : ℝ^P → ℝ such that ‖Dg'(x)‖ ≤ K for every x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ g' x), |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ for every x, and g'(x) = c whenever x ∈ ℝ^P and c ∈ ℝ are such that g(y) = c for every y in the open ball B_σ(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (K : NNReal) (σ : ℝ), LipschitzWith K g → 0 < σ → ∃ g' : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g' ∧ (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ g' x‖ ≤ K) ∧ (∀ x, |g' x - g x| ≤ K * σ) ∧ ∀ (x : Euclid P) (c : ℝ), (∀ y ∈ ball x σ, g y = c) → g' x = c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.8–4.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 1401–1402: to handle general Lipschitz f use f^(σ) in place of f), and step 3 of the parent proof (f_σ := f ∗ φ_σ is C^∞, |∇f_σ| ≤ L, |f_σ − f| ≤ Lσ); the locality property records that mollification at scale σ only sees the values of g on B_σ(x). Let λ := volume, Lebesgue measure on ℝ^P = Euclid P, an additive Haar measure (translation invariant, invariant under x ↦ −x, locally finite and positive on nonempty open sets).
1. (Mollifier.) Let φ be a C^∞ bump function centred at 0 with inner radius σ/2 and outer radius σ (a ContDiffBump (0 : Euclid P), available by hasContDiffBump_of_innerProductSpace) and ψ := φ.normed λ. Then ψ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff_normed), ψ ≥ 0 (nonneg_normed), ∫ ψ dλ = 1 (integral_normed), support ψ = B_σ(0) (support_normed_eq) and ψ has compact support (hasCompactSupport_normed).
2. (Definition.) Put g' := ψ ⋆ g (Mathlib convolution with lsmul ℝ ℝ and λ), g'(x) = ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y). For every x the integrand is continuous with compact support (contained in the closed ball of radius σ), hence integrable.
3. (Smoothness.) g is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ψ is C^∞ with compact support, so g' is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
4. (Gradient bound.) For x, x' ∈ ℝ^P, g'(x) − g'(x') = ∫ ψ(y)·(g(x − y) − g(x' − y)) dλ(y) (integral_sub) and |g(x − y) − g(x' − y)| ≤ K‖x − x'‖, so |g'(x) − g'(x')| ≤ ∫ ψ(y)·K‖x − x'‖ dλ(y) = K‖x − x'‖ (ψ ≥ 0, ∫ψ dλ = 1). Thus g' is K-Lipschitz, and since g' is differentiable, ‖fderiv ℝ g' x‖ ≤ K for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
5. (Uniform approximation.) Fix x. For x' ∈ B_σ(x), dist(g(x'), g(x)) ≤ K‖x' − x‖ ≤ K·σ. Since φ has outer radius σ and g is a.e. strongly measurable (continuous), ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le with ε := K·σ gives |g'(x) − g(x)| ≤ K·σ.
6. (Locality.) Suppose g(y) = c for every y ∈ B_σ(x). Then g(x) = c and g(y) = g(x) on the ball of radius φ.rOut = σ about x, so ContDiffBump.normed_convolution_eq_right gives g'(x) = g(x) = c. (Directly: for y ∈ support ψ = B_σ(0), x − y ∈ B_σ(x), so g(x − y) = c and g'(x) = c·∫ψ dλ = c.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Convolve g with a normalized smooth bump ψ supported in B_σ(0) (ContDiffBump.normed).
The convolution is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
It is K-Lipschitz, so ‖Dg'‖ ≤ K (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
|g' − g| ≤ Kσ (dist_normed_convolution_le) and g'(x) = c when g ≡ c on B_σ(x) (normed_convolution_eq_right).

audit.reason: Normalized compactly supported convolution supplies smoothness, preserves the Lipschitz constant, and gives both uniform approximation and open-ball locality. All needed measure and finite-dimensional hypotheses hold, including P = 0.

subproblem.title: Integrated slice-mass bound from the pointwise bound (Simon Ch. 6, 4.10)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, W ⊆ ℝ^P measurable, L ≥ 0, m : ℝ → [0, ∞] an arbitrary function and a, b ∈ ℝ. Suppose m(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every t ∈ (a, b). Then the lower Lebesgue integral satisfies ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m(t) dt ≤ L·μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (a b : ℝ), Measurable f → MeasurableSet W → (∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, m t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, m t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.10 and the remark preceding it (chapter-06.txt lines 1367–1376: M_W(T⌞{f<t}) is increasing in t, hence differentiable for L¹-a.e. t, ∫_a^b (d/dt)M_W(T⌞{f<t}) dt ≤ M_W(T⌞{a<f<b}), and 4.9 gives 4.10), and step 4 of the parent proof; μ(W ∩ {a < f < s}) plays the role of M_W(T⌞{a<f<s}) and m(t) that of M_W(⟨T, f, t₋⟩). Write S_h(t) := {x : t − h < f(x) < t} and N := μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
1. (Trivial cases.) If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ and the left side is 0. If L = 0, the hypothesis gives m(t) ≤ 0·(…) = 0 for every t ∈ (a, b) (in [0, ∞], 0·∞ = 0), so m = 0 a.e. for volume restricted to Ioo a b (ae_restrict_iff' with measurableSet_Ioo) and the left side is 0 (lintegral_mono_ae). If L > 0 and N = ∞, the right side is ∞. Assume from now on a < b and N < ∞.
2. (Distribution function.) For s ∈ ℝ let E_s := W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)} and F(s) := (μ(E_s)).toReal. If s ≤ s' then E_s ⊆ E_{s'}, and μ(E_s) ≤ μ(E_b) = N < ∞; hence F is real valued and monotone on ℝ, ofReal(F(s)) = μ(E_s), F(s) = 0 for s ≤ a (then E_s = ∅) and F(b) = N.toReal.
3. (Strip estimate.) Let t ∈ (a, b) and 0 < h < t − a. E_t = W ∩ {a < f < t} is the disjoint union of W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} and W ∩ S_h(t), and W ∩ S_h(t) is measurable (W and f are measurable). By additivity (measure_union), μ(E_t) = μ(W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≥ μ(E_{t−h}) + μ(W ∩ S_h(t)), because E_{t−h} = W ∩ {a < f < t − h} ⊆ W ∩ {a < f ≤ t − h} (note t − h < b). All terms are finite, so μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(F(t) − F(t − h)) and ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h).
4. (Differentiation.) F is monotone, so by Lebesgue's theorem (Monotone.ae_differentiableAt) it is differentiable at a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Let t ∈ (a, b) be such a point. By hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope, (F(s) − F(t))/(s − t) → deriv F t as s → t, s ≠ t; with s = t − h and h → 0+ this says (F(t) − F(t − h))/h → deriv F t, hence ofReal((F(t) − F(t − h))/h) → ofReal(deriv F t). By step 3 (valid for all h ∈ (0, t − a), i.e. eventually in 𝓝[>]0), liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h(t)) ≤ ofReal(deriv F t), and by hypothesis m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t). Thus m(t) ≤ L·ofReal(deriv F t) for a.e. t ∈ (a, b).
5. (Integration.) By lintegral_mono_ae (valid for arbitrary, not necessarily measurable, functions) for volume restricted to Ioo a b, and lintegral_const_mul' (L ≠ ∞), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ ∫⁻_{(a,b)} L·ofReal(deriv F t) dt = L·∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt. deriv F ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg) and deriv F is integrable on [a, b] (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), so ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F) = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal), and ∫_{(a,b)} deriv F = ∫_{(a,b]} deriv F = ∫_a^b deriv F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le) ≤ F(b) − F(a) = N.toReal (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, uIcc a b = [a, b], F(a) = 0). Hence ∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ L·ofReal(N.toReal) = L·N, since N < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dispose of b ≤ a, L = 0 and μ(W ∩ {a<f<b}) = ∞.
F(s) := μ(W ∩ {a < f < min(s, b)}).toReal is monotone and μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t−h) for t ∈ (a, b), 0 < h < t − a.
At a.e. t (Lebesgue: monotone F is differentiable a.e.) the liminf is ≤ F'(t), so m(t) ≤ L·F'(t) a.e. on (a, b).
∫⁻_{(a,b)} m ≤ L·∫_a^b F' ≤ L·(F(b) − F(a)) = L·μ(W ∩ {a<f<b}) (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc).

audit.reason: The finite truncated distribution function supplies the strip bound and an almost-everywhere derivative majorant. Monotone differentiation and derivative integrability prove the stated lower-integral estimate without assuming measurability of m. Degenerate cases are covered.

subproblem.title: Restriction of a measure-represented current to an arbitrary set is a current (Simon Ch. 6, 2.9)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, for μ-a.e. x (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α, the Euclidean coefficient norm), and let E ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Then there is a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) with S(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (Bochner integral for μ restricted to E) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = ∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 283–288: T⌞A(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω, T⃗⟩ dμ_T) and step 1 of the parent proof, here for an arbitrary representation (μ, ξ) and an arbitrary set E. For a test form ω write ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) for its underlying form, and put ν := μ.restrict E, so that ∫_E G dμ = ∫ G dν. Since ν ≤ μ (Measure.restrict_le_self), ν(K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and every μ-a.e. property holds ν-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae).
1. (Norm comparison.) Let N be the number of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P and C := √N. For every n-covector α and every such I, |α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖α‖ (le_opNorm for the continuous alternating map α; the standard basis vectors have norm 1). Hence |α|² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² ≤ N·‖α‖², i.e. |α| ≤ C‖α‖.
2. (Integrability.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). K := tsupport ω̂ is compact (ω̂ has compact support) and K ⊆ U, so μ(K) < ∞; ω̂ is continuous with compact support, so M_ω := sup_x ‖ω̂(x)‖ < ∞. The integrand F_ω(x) := ξ(x)(ω̂(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: it is the continuous evaluation map (Λ, α) ↦ Λ(α) on MultiVector P n × Λⁿ (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply) composed with the a.e. strongly measurable ξ and the continuous ω̂ (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂). For μ-a.e. x, |F_ω(x)| ≤ |ω̂(x)| ≤ C‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ C·M_ω·1_K(x), because ω̂(x) = 0 for x ∉ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ξ(x)(0) = 0. Then ∂A(η) = B(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose topological support tsupport η is disjoint from {x : f(x) = t}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.8 (chapter-06.txt line 1353; Simon derives it from 4.11, lines 1378–1394) and step 2 of the parent proof, which proves it directly by splitting η. For a form θ write θ̂ for its underlying map ℝ^P → Λ. Recall ∂A(η) = A(dη), where dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η has underlying form exteriorDerivative η̂ (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); likewise ∂T(θ) = T(dθ).
1. (Vanishing principle.) If θ is a form and x ∉ tsupport θ̂, then θ̂(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and (exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x) = 0, because tsupport (exteriorDerivative θ̂) ⊆ tsupport θ̂ (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). For any set S, measure ν and G : ℝ^P → ℝ: if G = 0 off S then ∫_S G dν = ∫ G dν (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and if G = 0 on S then ∫_S G dν = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero); neither needs integrability. Every ξ(x), ξ'(x) is linear, so it maps 0 to 0.
2. (Separation of the support.) Let η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport η̂ ∩ {f = t} = ∅ and K := tsupport η̂, a compact subset of U. If K = ∅ then η̂ = 0, η = 0 and ∂A(η) = 0 = B(η) by linearity. Otherwise f(K) is a nonempty compact subset of ℝ not containing t, so δ := dist(t, f(K))/2 > 0 and every x ∈ K satisfies f(x) ≤ t − 2δ or f(x) ≥ t + 2δ. The sets C₋ := {f ≤ t − δ} and C₊ := {f ≥ t + δ} are closed (f is continuous) and disjoint. By the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib exists_contDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed with s := C₊ and t := C₋) there is a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 0 on C₊ and χ = 1 on C₋.
3. (Splitting η.) Let η̂₋(x) := χ(x)·η̂(x) and η̂₊(x) := (1 − χ(x))·η̂(x). Both are C^∞ (products of smooth maps) and vanish wherever η̂ does, so their topological supports lie in the compact set K ⊆ U; hence they define η₋, η₊ ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and η = η₋ + η₊. Moreover {η̂₋ ≠ 0} ⊆ {χ ≠ 0} ∩ K ⊆ {f < t + δ} ∩ K = K ∩ {f ≤ t − 2δ}, a closed set, so tsupport η̂₋ ⊆ K ∩ {f ≤ t − 2δ} ⊆ {f < t}. Similarly {η̂₊ ≠ 0} ⊆ {χ ≠ 1} ∩ K ⊆ {f > t − δ} ∩ K = K ∩ {f ≥ t + 2δ}, closed, so tsupport η̂₊ ⊆ {f > t}.
4. (The part above the level.) If f(x) < t then x ∉ tsupport η̂₊, so by step 1 η̂₊(x) = 0 and (exteriorDerivative η̂₊)(x) = 0; thus the integrands ξ(x)(dη̂₊(x)) and ξ'(x)(η̂₊(x)) vanish on {f < t}, and ∂A(η₊) = A(dη₊) = ∫_{{f<t}} ξ(dη̂₊) dμ = 0 and B(η₊) = ∫_{{f<t}} ξ'(η̂₊) dμ' = 0.
5. (The part below the level.) If f(x) ≥ t then x ∉ tsupport η̂₋, so η̂₋ and exteriorDerivative η̂₋ vanish at x; the integrands ξ(x)(dη̂₋(x)) and ξ'(x)(η̂₋(x)) vanish off {f < t}. By step 1, the representation of T, the definition of the boundary and the representation of ∂T:
∂A(η₋) = ∫_{{f<t}} ξ(dη̂₋) dμ = ∫ ξ(dη̂₋) dμ = T(dη₋) = ∂T(η₋) = ∫ ξ'(η̂₋) dμ' = ∫_{{f<t}} ξ'(η̂₋) dμ' = B(η₋).
6. (Conclusion.) ∂A and B are linear, so ∂A(η) = ∂A(η₋) + ∂A(η₊) = B(η₋) + 0 = B(η₋) + B(η₊) = B(η). ∎

A smooth Urysohn function χ (1 on {f ≤ t − δ}, 0 on {f ≥ t + δ}) splits η = χη + (1 − χ)η into test forms with supports in {f < t} and {f > t}.
On the upper part both ∂A and B vanish, because the integrands vanish on {f < t}.
On the lower part ∂A(η₋) = T(dη₋) = ∂T(η₋) = B(η₋), because the integrands vanish off {f < t}; add by linearity.

subproblem.title: Smooth cut-off of a sublevel set of a Lipschitz function, gradient ≤ L/(h(1 − h/2)) and supported in the strip {t − h < f < t}
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, t ∈ ℝ and 0 < h < 1. Then there is a C^∞ function g : ℝ^P → ℝ such that |g(x)| ≤ 2 for all x; ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ L/(h(1 − h/2)) for all x (operator norm of fderiv ℝ g x); Dg(x) ≠ 0 implies t − h < f(x) < t; g(x) = 1 whenever f(x) ≤ t − h; and g(x) = 0 whenever f(x) ≥ t.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (t h : ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → 0 < h → h < 1 → ∃ g : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g ∧ (∀ x, |g x| ≤ 2) ∧ (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ ≤ L / (h * (1 - h / 2))) ∧ (∀ x, fderiv ℝ g x ≠ 0 → t - h < f x ∧ f x < t) ∧ (∀ x, f x ≤ t - h → g x = 1) ∧ (∀ x, t ≤ f x → g x = 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 4.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1402: a cut-off γ∘f with γ = 1 below a, γ = 0 above b and |γ'| ≤ (1+ε)/(b − a), used with f^(σ) in place of f when f is only Lipschitz), and step 3 of the parent proof (ε := h²/8, smooth γ with |γ'| ≤ 1/(h − 4ε) = 1/(h(1 − h/2)), g_σ := γ∘f_σ). Departure: here the profile γ is piecewise linear and the smoothing (sibling cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing) is applied to γ∘f instead of to f; this produces one smooth function with the same constant L/(h(1 − h/2)), the same localisation of Dg and the same plateaus, without constructing a separate smooth profile.
1. (Parameters.) δ := h²/4. Since 0 < h < 1, h − 2δ = h(1 − h/2) > 0. Let σ := δ/(2(L + 1)) > 0; then 2Lσ = Lδ/(L + 1) < δ.
2. (Profile.) γ(s) := max(0, min(1, (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ))) for s ∈ ℝ. Then 0 ≤ γ ≤ 1; γ(s) = 1 if s ≤ t − h + δ (then (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ) ≥ 1); γ(s) = 0 if s ≥ t − δ. γ is Lipschitz with constant (h − 2δ)⁻¹, as the composition of the affine map s ↦ (t − δ − s)/(h − 2δ) (Lipschitz constant (h − 2δ)⁻¹) with the 1-Lipschitz clamp r ↦ max(0, min(1, r)). Hence G := γ∘f is Lipschitz with constant K := L·(h − 2δ)⁻¹ = L/(h(1 − h/2)) (LipschitzWith.comp), 0 ≤ G ≤ 1, G(y) = 1 when f(y) ≤ t − h + δ and G(y) = 0 when f(y) ≥ t − δ.
3. (Smoothing.) The sibling cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing applied to G, K and σ gives a C^∞ function g : ℝ^P → ℝ with ‖Dg(x)‖ ≤ K = L/(h(1 − h/2)) for all x, |g(x) − G(x)| ≤ K·σ for all x, and g(x') = c whenever G = c on B_σ(x'). This gives smoothness and the gradient bound.
4. (|g| ≤ 2.) K·σ = Lδ/(2(L + 1)(h − 2δ)) ≤ δ/(2(h − 2δ)) = h²/(8h(1 − h/2)) = h/(8(1 − h/2)) < 1/4, because h < 1 and 1 − h/2 > 1/2. Hence |g(x)| ≤ |G(x)| + K·σ ≤ 1 + 1/4 ≤ 2.
5. (Lower plateau.) Let f(x) ≤ t − h. For x' ∈ B_σ(x) and y ∈ B_σ(x') we have ‖y − x‖ < 2σ, so f(y) ≤ f(x) + L‖y − x‖ ≤ t − h + 2Lσ < t − h + δ and G(y) = 1. By the locality in step 3, g(x') = 1 for every x' ∈ B_σ(x). Thus g = 1 on the open ball B_σ(x), so g(x) = 1 and Dg(x) = 0 (g agrees near x with a constant: Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq and fderiv_const).
6. (Upper plateau.) Let f(x) ≥ t. For x', y as in step 5, f(y) ≥ f(x) − L‖y − x‖ ≥ t − 2Lσ > t − δ, so G(y) = 0; hence g = 0 on B_σ(x), so g(x) = 0 and Dg(x) = 0.
7. (Transition strip.) If Dg(x) ≠ 0, then by steps 5 and 6 neither f(x) ≤ t − h nor f(x) ≥ t, i.e. t − h < f(x) < t. Steps 3–7 give all the claimed properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take δ = h²/4, the piecewise-linear profile γ (1 below t − h + δ, 0 above t − δ, slope (h − 2δ)⁻¹) and G = γ∘f, which is L/(h(1 − h/2))-Lipschitz.
Smooth G at scale σ = δ/(2(L+1)) with cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing: gradient bound, |g − G| ≤ 1/4, locality.
If f(x) ≤ t − h (resp. f(x) ≥ t), G ≡ 1 (resp. 0) on B_{2σ}(x), so g ≡ 1 (resp. 0) on B_σ(x) and Dg(x) = 0.
Hence Dg(x) ≠ 0 forces t − h < f(x) < t.

subproblem.title: Coefficient norm of the wedge of a 1-form with a k-covector: |β ∧ γ| ≤ ‖β‖·|γ| (fact (E1) behind Simon Ch. 6, 4.11)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let β : ℝ^P → ℝ be a continuous linear functional with operator norm ‖β‖ and γ a k-covector on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) k). Let β ∧ γ be the (k+1)-covector ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ), i.e. (β ∧ γ)(v_0, …, v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i·β(v_i)·γ(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_k). Then |β ∧ γ| ≤ ‖β‖·|γ|, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is the Euclidean coefficient norm |α| = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(m−1)})²)^{1/2} of an m-covector α (e the standard basis of ℝ^P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (β : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (γ : Covector (Euclid P) k), covectorEuclideanNorm (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ)) ≤ ‖β‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (E1) of the parent proof (|β ∧ γ| ≤ |β||γ|, proved there by rotating β to a multiple of a basis vector), with Simon's wedge product (Ch. 6, 1.1–1.3, chapter-06.txt lines 26–60) and Euclidean norm (1.15, line 178). We use the sibling regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, denoted (Σ): for every m ∈ ℕ, every m-covector α and every orthonormal basis f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = m!·|α|², where f∘j := (f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(m−1)}).
Put ω := alternatizeUncurryFin (β.smulRight γ). By alternatizeUncurryFin_apply and (β.smulRight γ)(v) = β(v)·γ, for every v : Fin (k+1) → ℝ^P we have ω(v) = Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} (−1)^i·β(v_i)·γ(Fin.removeNth i v).
1. (Riesz representative.) Let b := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Euclid P)).symm β. Then β(v) = ⟨b, v⟩ for every v (toDual_symm_apply) and ‖b‖ = ‖β‖ (toDual is a linear isometry equivalence).
2. (Case b = 0.) Then β = 0, so β.smulRight γ = 0 and ω = 0 (alternatizeUncurryFin is the continuous linear map alternatizeUncurryFinCLM, which maps 0 to 0). Hence |ω| = 0 ≤ ‖β‖·|γ| (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero, |γ| ≥ 0). From now on b ≠ 0; then ℝ^P ≠ {0}, so P ≥ 1 and 0 ∈ Fin P.
3. (An orthonormal basis adapted to b.) Let u := ‖b‖⁻¹·b, so ‖u‖ = 1, and let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ. Let R := reflection (ℝ ∙ (e_0 − u))ᗮ, a linear isometry equivalence of ℝ^P; since ‖e_0‖ = 1 = ‖u‖, R(e_0) = u (reflection_sub). The family f := e.map R (OrthonormalBasis.map), f_i = R(e_i), is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P with f_0 = u. By orthonormality β(f_i) = ⟨b, f_i⟩ = ‖b‖·⟨f_0, f_i⟩, which equals ‖b‖ for i = 0 and 0 for i ≠ 0.
4. (Values on basis tuples.) Let j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P; note Fin.removeNth i (f∘j) = f∘(Fin.removeNth i j). By step 3, ω(f∘j) = ‖b‖·Σ_{i : j(i) = 0} (−1)^i·γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j)).
(a) If j is not injective, then f∘j is not injective (f is injective), so ω(f∘j) = 0 because ω is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
(b) If j is injective, at most one index i has j(i) = 0, so the sum has at most one term and ω(f∘j)² = ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : j(i) = 0} γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))².
Hence in all cases (∗) ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} [j(i) = 0]·γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))², since in case (a) the left side is 0 and the right side is a sum of squares.
5. (Summation.) Summing (∗) over all j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P and exchanging the finite sums, Σ_j ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·Σ_{i : Fin (k+1)} Σ_{j : j(i) = 0} γ(f∘(Fin.removeNth i j))². For fixed i, j ↦ Fin.removeNth i j is a bijection from {j : Fin (k+1) → Fin P | j(i) = 0} onto Fin k → Fin P with inverse j' ↦ Fin.insertNth i 0 j' (Fin.removeNth_insertNth, and Fin.insertNth_self_removeNth together with j(i) = 0). So the inner sum equals Σ_{j' : Fin k → Fin P} γ(f∘j')² = k!·|γ|² by (Σ) with m = k. Therefore Σ_j ω(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖²·(k+1)·k!·|γ|² = (k+1)!·‖b‖²·|γ|².
6. (Conclusion.) By (Σ) with m = k+1 and α = ω, Σ_j ω(f∘j)² = (k+1)!·|ω|². Hence (k+1)!·|ω|² ≤ (k+1)!·(‖b‖·|γ|)², and since (k+1)! > 0, |ω|² ≤ (‖b‖·|γ|)². Both |ω| and ‖b‖·|γ| are nonnegative (covectorEuclideanNorm is a square root), so |ω| ≤ ‖b‖·|γ| = ‖β‖·|γ| (sq_le_sq₀: for nonnegative reals a² ≤ c² ↔ a ≤ c). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write β = ⟨b, ·⟩ with ‖b‖ = ‖β‖; the case b = 0 is trivial.
Choose an orthonormal basis f with f_0 = b/‖b‖ (reflection of the standard basis), so β(f_i) = ‖b‖δ_{i0}.
On basis tuples, (β∧γ)(f∘j)² ≤ ‖b‖² Σ_i [j(i) = 0] γ(f∘removeNth i j)² (non-injective tuples give 0).
Summing and using removeNth/insertNth bijections and the basis-invariant square sum (Σ) twice gives (k+1)!|β∧γ|² ≤ (k+1)!‖b‖²|γ|².

subproblem.title: Simon's identity 4.11 with its mass estimate: |T(g dη) − ∂T(gη)| = |T(dg ∧ η)| ≤ ∫ ‖Dg‖·|η| dμ
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), μ, μ' measures on ℝ^P, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) such that |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all (k+1)-covectors α for μ-a.e. x, T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for all θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ and η ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then, in [0, ∞], ofReal |∫ g(x)·ξ(x)(dη(x)) dμ(x) − ∫ g(x)·ξ'(x)(η(x)) dμ'(x)| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(‖Dg(x)‖·|η(x)|) dμ(x), where dη = exteriorDerivative η, ‖Dg(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ g x and |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (k + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, T.boundary θ = ∫ x, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → ENNReal.ofReal |∫ x, g x * ξ x (exteriorDerivative (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ - ∫ x, g x * ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ'| ≤ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (‖fderiv ℝ g x‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x)) ∂μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 1378–1386: ∂(T⌞γ∘f)(ω) − (∂T)⌞γ∘f(ω) = T(γ∘f dω) − T(d(γ∘f ω)) = −T(γ'(f) df ∧ ω)) with the estimate of its right side (lines 1394–1399), and steps 3(i)–(ii) of the parent proof; here for an arbitrary smooth g in place of γ∘f. The wedge estimate (E1) is the sibling cmcs_wedge_norm_le: |alternatizeUncurryFin(β.smulRight γ)| ≤ ‖β‖·|γ| for every continuous linear β : ℝ^P → ℝ and every k-covector γ. Write η̂ for the underlying form of η and dη̂ := exteriorDerivative η̂ (Mathlib extDeriv); K := tsupport η̂ is a compact subset of U.
1. (Leibniz rule.) For every x, g and η̂ are differentiable at x, so fderiv ℝ (y ↦ g(y)·η̂(y)) x = g(x)·fderiv ℝ η̂ x + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight(η̂(x)) (fderiv_fun_smul). By definition, extDeriv θ x = alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ θ x), and alternatizeUncurryFin is additive and commutes with real scalars (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_add, alternatizeUncurryFin_smul). Hence for every x, d(gη̂)(x) = g(x)·dη̂(x) + D(x), where D(x) := alternatizeUncurryFin((fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight(η̂(x))).
2. (Test forms.) The forms η̂_g(x) := g(x)·η̂(x) and ω̂_g(x) := g(x)·dη̂(x) are C^∞ (products of smooth maps; dη̂ is smooth by SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_isTestForm) and vanish wherever η̂, resp. dη̂, vanishes, so their topological supports lie in K (tsupport dη̂ ⊆ tsupport η̂ by tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Hence they define η_g ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and ω_g ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U). Since 𝒟^{k+1}(U) is a submodule, D_T := dη_g − ω_g ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U), where dη_g := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η_g; by step 1 its underlying form is D.
3. (Rewriting the left side.) Every ξ(x), ξ'(x) is linear, so ξ(x)(ω̂_g(x)) = g(x)·ξ(x)(dη̂(x)) and ξ'(x)(η̂_g(x)) = g(x)·ξ'(x)(η̂(x)) for all x. By the two representations (and integral_congr, which needs no integrability), ∫ g·ξ(dη̂) dμ = T(ω_g) and ∫ g·ξ'(η̂) dμ' = ∂T(η_g) = T(dη_g). Since T is linear on 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and dη_g = ω_g + D_T, T(ω_g) − T(dη_g) = −T(D_T) = −∫ ξ(x)(D(x)) dμ(x).
4. (Integral bound.) For every real function G, ofReal|∫ G dμ| = ‖∫ G dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖G‖ₑ dμ = ∫⁻ ofReal|G| dμ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs; if G is not integrable the left side is 0). With G := ξ(·)(D(·)) and step 3, ofReal|∫ g·ξ(dη̂) dμ − ∫ g·ξ'(η̂) dμ'| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|ξ(x)(D(x))| dμ(x).
5. (Pointwise bound.) For μ-a.e. x the hypothesis on ξ gives |ξ(x)(D(x))| ≤ |D(x)|, and the sibling cmcs_wedge_norm_le with β := fderiv ℝ g x and γ := η̂(x) gives |D(x)| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ g x‖·|η̂(x)|. Since ofReal is monotone, lintegral_mono_ae gives ∫⁻ ofReal|ξ(D)| dμ ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(‖Dg(x)‖·|η̂(x)|) dμ(x). Together with step 4 this is the claim. ∎

gη, g dη and their difference dg∧η = d(gη) − g dη are test forms in U.
By the representations, ∫ g ξ(dη) dμ − ∫ g ξ'(η) dμ' = T(g dη) − T(d(gη)) = −T(dg∧η) = −∫ ξ(dg∧η) dμ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 4.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 1355–1366) with its proof from 4.11 (lines 1378–1402), and step 3 of the parent proof. Departure: the parent first lets σ ↓ 0 for fixed h and then lets h ↓ 0; here, for each h, the sibling cmcs_level_cutoff supplies one smooth cut-off g_h (smoothed at an h-dependent scale), so a single limit h ↓ 0 suffices. Siblings used: cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound and cmcs_level_cutoff. Notation: |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm; θ̂ is the underlying form of a test form θ; dθ̂ := exteriorDerivative θ̂; S_h := {x : t − h < f(x) < t}.
1. (Reduction.) By definition, (∂A − B).massOn W is the supremum of ofReal((∂A − B)(η)) over the admissible η, i.e. η ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport η̂ ⊆ W and |η̂(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So (sSup_le) it suffices to fix an admissible η and prove ofReal(Z) ≤ R, where Z := (∂A − B)(η) and R := L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h). By the definitions of subtraction of currents and of the boundary, Z = A(dη) − B(η) = ∫_{{f<t}} F dμ − ∫_{{f<t}} F' dμ', where F(x) := ξ(x)(dη̂(x)) and F'(x) := ξ'(x)(η̂(x)).
2. (Integrability.) K₀ := tsupport η̂ is compact and K₀ ⊆ U, so μ(K₀) < ∞ and μ'(K₀) < ∞. The maps η̂ and dη̂ are continuous and vanish outside K₀ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). The coefficient norm is continuous (each α ↦ α(e∘I) is continuous linear and √ is continuous), so M := sup_x |dη̂(x)| < ∞; also |η̂| ≤ 1. By the hypotheses on ξ, ξ', |F| ≤ M·1_{K₀} μ-a.e. and |F'| ≤ 1_{K₀} μ'-a.e. F and F' are a.e. strongly measurable (the continuous evaluation (Λ, α) ↦ Λ(α), isBoundedBilinearMap_apply, composed with the a.e. strongly measurable ξ, resp. ξ', and a continuous form; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂). Hence F ∈ L¹(μ) and F' ∈ L¹(μ').
3. (Cut-offs.) For h ∈ (0, 1) let g_h be given by the sibling cmcs_level_cutoff for f, L, t, h: g_h is C^∞, |g_h| ≤ 2, ‖Dg_h(x)‖ ≤ c_h := L/(h(1 − h/2)), Dg_h(x) ≠ 0 ⇒ x ∈ S_h, g_h = 1 on {f ≤ t − h} and g_h = 0 on {f ≥ t}. (For h ∉ (0, 1) put g_h := 0; only h ∈ (0, 1) matters for limits along 𝓝[>]0.)
4. (Estimate for fixed h ∈ (0, 1).) Let Φ_h := ∫ g_h·F dμ − ∫ g_h·F' dμ'. The sibling cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound (with g := g_h and our η) gives ofReal|Φ_h| ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(‖Dg_h(x)‖·|η̂(x)|) dμ(x). For every x the integrand is ≤ (K₀ ∩ S_h).indicator (ofReal c_h) at x: if x ∉ K₀ then η̂(x) = 0 and |η̂(x)| = 0; if Dg_h(x) = 0 the integrand is 0; otherwise x ∈ K₀ ∩ S_h and ‖Dg_h(x)‖·|η̂(x)| ≤ c_h·1. By lintegral_mono, lintegral_indicator_const_le and monotonicity of μ (K₀ ⊆ W), ofReal|Φ_h| ≤ ofReal(c_h)·μ(K₀ ∩ S_h) ≤ ofReal(c_h)·μ(W ∩ S_h).
5. (Limit h → 0+.) The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is countably generated and nontrivial. For every x, g_h(x) → 1_{{f<t}}(x) along 𝓝[>]0: if f(x) < t then g_h(x) = 1 for 0 < h ≤ min(t − f(x), 1/2); if f(x) ≥ t then g_h(x) = 0 for all h ∈ (0, 1). For h ∈ (0, 1), g_h·F is a.e. strongly measurable (g_h is continuous) and |g_h·F| ≤ 2|F|, with 2|F| integrable; likewise for F'. By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ g_h·F dμ → ∫ 1_{{f<t}}·F dμ = ∫_{{f<t}} F dμ and ∫ g_h·F' dμ' → ∫_{{f<t}} F' dμ' ({f < t} is open, hence measurable; integral_indicator). Hence Φ_h → Z and ofReal|Φ_h| → ofReal|Z| (continuity of ofReal ∘ |·|).
6. (Passing to the liminf.) Since 𝓝[>]0 is nontrivial, ofReal(Z) ≤ ofReal|Z| = liminf_{h→0+} ofReal|Φ_h| ≤ liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(c_h)·μ(W ∩ S_h), using step 4 for all h ∈ (0, 1), i.e. eventually (liminf_le_liminf). For h ∈ (0, 1), c_h = (1 − h/2)⁻¹·L·h⁻¹ with nonnegative factors, so ofReal(c_h) = a_h·L·ofReal(h⁻¹) with a_h := ofReal((1 − h/2)⁻¹) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul; ofReal of the real coercion of L is L). Put u_h := ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ S_h); the last liminf is liminf_{h→0+} a_h·(L·u_h). Let r > 1 be real. Since a_h → ofReal 1 = 1 as h → 0+, eventually a_h ≤ ofReal r, so liminf a_h·(L·u_h) ≤ liminf ofReal(r)·L·u_h = ofReal(r)·L·liminf u_h (ENNReal.liminf_const_mul_of_ne_top, ofReal(r)·L ≠ ∞). If L·liminf u_h = ∞, then R = ∞ and ofReal(Z) ≤ R is trivial; otherwise letting r ↓ 1 gives liminf a_h·(L·u_h) ≤ L·liminf u_h = R. Hence ofReal(Z) ≤ R.
7. (Conclusion.) Step 6 holds for every admissible η; taking the supremum, (∂A − B).massOn W ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible η: Z = ∫_{f<t} ξ(dη) dμ − ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ', with integrable integrands.
For h ∈ (0,1), the cut-off g_h of cmcs_level_cutoff and cmcs_cutoff_defect_bound give ofReal|Φ_h| ≤ ofReal(L/(h(1 − h/2)))·μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}), Φ_h := ∫ g_h ξ(dη) dμ − ∫ g_h ξ'(η) dμ'.
g_h → 1_{f<t} pointwise with |g_h| ≤ 2, so Φ_h → Z by dominated convergence along 𝓝[>]0.
Pass to the liminf and remove the factor (1 − h/2)⁻¹ → 1; take the supremum over admissible η.

audit.reason: Compact domination justifies filter dominated convergence. The cutoff defect bounds every admissible evaluation; the ENNReal liminf argument removes the extra factor correctly, including zero constants and infinite measures. Taking the supremum gives exactly massOn.
